title: Kimbap: A Node-Property Map System for Distributed Graph Analytics
problem: Existing distributed graph analytics systems only support computational models where node properties are updated using adjacent neighbor properties, preventing expression of algorithms like Louvain for community detection and Shiloach-Vishkin for connected components.
motivation: These restricted algorithms may be less efficient or produce lower quality results than algorithms with more flexible property access patterns.
method: Existing distributed graph systems only allow nodes to update properties using data from neighboring nodes. Kimbap introduces a 'Node-Property Map' abstraction that removes this restriction, letting nodes access and modify any properties during iterative computation. This enables previously impossible algorithms like Louvain (which identifies communities) and Shiloach-Vishkin (which finds connected components). The system maintains efficient parallel execution across multiple machines.
key_novelty: Kimbap's Node-Property Map abstraction lets graph algorithms freely access any node properties, instead of limiting them to neighboring nodes' data.
